title: Arrears Payment Amount Toward an Extension — Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Worked Sheet
content:
**Servicing Training worked sheet — Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

## The other past-due amount

The other past-due amount is the contract's past-due amount less one monthly payment for each installment the most recent completed signed extension agreement on the contract defers, those being its oldest installments; when two completed agreements carry the same creation time, the one recorded first is read. This policy applies only where a completed signed extension agreement is on the contract; without one there is no arrears payment under this policy.

The installments an agreement defers are the installments requested on that completed signed extension agreement; "most recent" is judged by the agreement's creation time.

## The amount

The arrears share is 100 percent, and the arrears payment amount is the arrears share of the other past-due amount, rounded to the cent. The arrears share is one percentage for the contract, applied once to the other past-due amount; the arrears payment amount is never below zero.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

Monthly payment 380.00 dollars; past-due amount 1,140.00 dollars (three installments); the most recent completed signed extension agreement requested 1 installment.

1. The other past-due amount is 1,140.00 less one monthly payment of 380.00, which is 760.00 dollars.
2. The arrears share of 100 percent applied to 760.00 dollars gives 760.00 dollars.
3. The arrears payment amount is 760.00 dollars.

Had the agreement requested 2 installments, the other past-due amount would be 1,140.00 less two monthly payments, 380.00 dollars, and the arrears payment amount 380.00 dollars.

*Tie (hypothetical):* two completed agreements on the contract carry the same creation time, the first recorded requesting 1 installment and the second 2; the first recorded is read, so one monthly payment is taken off.
